title: An affirmative answer to Owings's sumset question
summary: We give an affirmative answer to Owings's sumset question: for any $2$-coloring of natural numbers, there is an infinite $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B$ is monochromatic. More generally, for every $m,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $2$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$, there is an infinite $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $$ (m+\ell)B\cup\{mx+\ell y:x,y\in B,\ x<y\} $$ is monochromatic.
